name: Inka chaski relay
summary: Inka chaski runners passed messages and small goods from runner to runner between roadside posts, letting the Inka state move news quickly along its roads.
description: State messengers handing news and small goods from runner to runner along selected Inka roads and roadside relay points.
tier_reason: Practice fits the messenger institution. Keep the relay distinct from the road and station architecture. This is a scoped consequence judgement, not a reward for documentation or representation.
why: The Inka ruled a long, mountainous empire without horses, so the state stationed trained runners along its roads to carry orders and news.

places.note: Andean regions of Tawantinsuyu (Inka empire), not limited to Peru and Chile

date.basis: The attributed Second Part describes an earlier Inka system; Cieza died in 1554. The relay chapter was printed only in the nineteenth century, not in the 1553 First Part.
